text:
support-alex: FYI ACME just opened an escalation — p95/p99 tail jumped after the continuous-batcher config push last night. Small prompts (~10 tokens) now 800-1200ms at p99. They've attached traces and a short cURL repro.

sam: ack. which config was pushed?

support-alex: we pushed 'continuous.hold_ms' 6 -> 12ms across hosted pool at 22:10 UTC. no other runtime changes.

lee: pinging infra metrics now. grabbing live histograms for tiny prompts.

maria: we also flipped adaptive-coalesce for that pool in the same deploy (opt-in). could be interaction.

lee: looking at token-level latency: batch wait time at p99 increased, but model compute roughly same. KV/cache hit rates unchanged. suggests batching hold tradeoff is holding single-request paths longer.

sam: can you paste the trace? want to confirm stage durations (queue vs model).

support-alex: trace snippet: 
```
trace_id: acme-2026-03-15-99
stages: receive:10ms -> wait_in_batch:920ms -> model_exec:60ms -> send:10ms
```

lee: yep that's wait_in_batch dominating. small requests getting stuck waiting for more peers that never arrive. hold_ms increase caused coalescer to prefer larger batches.

maria: that explains p95 rise. p50 unaffected. classic tail tradeoff.

sam: reproduce locally:
```
for i in 1..100:
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/outputs >/dev/null
```
Run in single-threaded bursts to mirror customer pattern. I see p99 ~900ms on canary.

lee: immediate mitigation options: 
- revert hold_ms to 6ms globally (fast)
- enable fastpath for single-token requests (deploy, needs QA)
- canary rollback to previous config for ACME's pool only (config flag per-tenant)

sre-oncall: I'm oncall, can perform emergency rollback to previous continuous config for hosted-prod pool.

sam: prefer scoped rollback for the pool serving ACME to avoid global perf churn. can we flip their pool flag?

maria: yes config flags are per-pool. I can flip ACME pool back to hold_ms=6 and disable adaptive-coalesce for them. doing it would be a 1-click via console but need owner ack.

support-alex: ACME wants quick fix, canary rollback ok. they prefer we avoid full service restart.

lee: before we flip, capture full debug traces for 5 minutes for SRE postmortem. also tag traces with cohort=acme-smallprompts.

sre-oncall: flipping ACME pool flag now. will monitor.

deploy-bot: [deploy] config-change: pool=acme-hosted hold_ms=6 adaptive_coalesce=off by maria @ 7132110210

maria: done. watch dashboards.

lee: dashboards show p99 dropped from ~1.1s to ~140ms within 90s. queue wait component gone.

support-alex: relaying to ACME — they confirm latency back to normal on their end. :white_check_mark:

sam: ok next steps:
- create runbook entry for hold_ms tradeoffs and thresholds for small-prompt heavy tenants
- add automated guardrail: if p99 for >95th percentile tiny-prompts increases >200ms within 5m after config change, auto-rollback scoped change
- follow-up postmortem with ACME traces attached

maria: opened ticket INF-7248 and added rollback timeline + logs.

sre-oncall: leaving notes on oncall log. no further action unless we see reappearance.

lee: one more ask — let's add a synthetic workload (tiny prompt burst) to canary suite to catch this in future. simple load test that sends sparse single-request bursts.

sam: agreed. I'll add it to the smoke pipeline.

support-alex: ACME thanked for quick response. closing the escalation once postmortem is up.

maria: postmortem draft in progress, will ping team for review.

sam: thanks all. moving to follow-ups. :thumbsup:
